title: AlphaEvolve finds a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices; Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic derive a rational-coefficient variant from its decomposition
summary: AlphaEvolve found a 48-multiplication 4x4 complex matrix algorithm (May 2025); Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic derived rational variants from its decomposition
account: On 14 May 2025 Google DeepMind announced AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent, and reported that it had found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 complex-valued matrices with 48 scalar multiplications, improving on the 49 obtained from two recursion levels of Strassen's 1969 algorithm. On 16 June 2025 Jean-Guillaume Dumas, Clément Pernet and Alexandre Sedoglavic (CASC and CRIStAL, France), researchers independent of DeepMind, posted a preprint presenting a 48-multiplication algorithm with only rational coefficients, removing the need for complex arithmetic; they state that it was derived from AlphaEvolve's algorithm under the action of an isotropy that projects the decomposition onto the field of rational numbers, so the derivation is not independent of the AI result and the preprint contains no explicit verification statement. On 19 March 2026 the same authors posted a more accurate variant of that rational algorithm, valid over any ring containing an inverse of 2. These derived variants corroborate and extend the rank-48 bound; the preprints are not yet recorded as journal-published.
purpose: Evolve and verify algorithms and constructions for open mathematical and computational problems

ratings.reason: Small: a research result for the developer; DeepMind's blog reports improvements on about 20% of the open problems tested
Small: a one-multiplication improvement for 4x4 matrices, since taken up by independent researchers in two preprints

ai_role.statement: AlphaEvolve discovered the 48-multiplication scheme over the complex numbers; researchers independent of DeepMind corroborated the rank-48 bound by deriving rational and more accurate variants from the AI's decomposition, through an isotropy that projects it onto the rational numbers, which is the community acceptance relied on here. The derivation is not independent of the AI result and the 2025 preprint does not state an explicit verification of it. Both sources are preprints by authors independent of DeepMind.
